_comment: Planner output for the two-slide Photosynthesis reference case, captured
as a fixture so composition can be tested without calling an LLM.
This is the CONTENT PLANNER / SLIDE STORYBOARD stage only: it says what
each slide teaches and what the learner should SEE, and deliberately says
nothing about layout, colour, image source or geometry. Everything from
'which layout' onwards is the composer's job, which is what makes it
subject: Science

slides.title: How Green Plants Make Their Own Food
slides.subtitle: Photosynthesis turns light into stored chemical energy
slides.learningObjective: Identify the four things a leaf needs in order to make food, and the two things it produces

blocks.label: Sunlight
blocks.text: Chlorophyll in the leaf traps energy from sunlight.

blocks.label: Water
blocks.text: Roots absorb water from the soil and carry it up to the leaves.

blocks.label: Carbon dioxide
blocks.text: Tiny pores called stomata let carbon dioxide into the leaf.

blocks.label: Food and oxygen
blocks.text: The leaf makes glucose and releases oxygen back into the air.

visual.description: a single broad green leaf on a stem, with sunlight falling on its upper surface, water rising through the stem, and gas moving at the leaf surface
visual.altText: A green leaf showing sunlight, water and carbon dioxide entering and oxygen leaving

slides.speakerNotes: Ask the class what a plant eats before revealing that it makes its own food. Point at each input on the diagram in turn.

slides.title: Photosynthesis Step by Step
slides.subtitle: The same reaction, as a sequence
slides.learningObjective: Put the stages of photosynthesis in the correct order

blocks.label: 2. Split
blocks.text: Light energy splits water into hydrogen and oxygen.

blocks.label: 3. Combine
blocks.text: Hydrogen joins carbon dioxide to form glucose.

blocks.label: 4. Release
blocks.text: Oxygen leaves the leaf through the stomata.

visual.description: energy conversion inside a chloroplast during photosynthesis
visual.altText: A chloroplast converting light energy into chemical energy

slides.speakerNotes: Emphasise that the oxygen comes from the water, not from the carbon dioxide. This is the step students most often get wrong.
